key_insight: Rotational equivariance improves subgrid-scale closure performance most when combined with nonlocal receptive fields, giving better generalization with fewer parameters.
engineering_relevance: For LES turbulence modeling, equivariant nonlocal closures can deliver more accurate and data-efficient SGS predictions across changing flow conditions and Reynolds numbers.
method: Compared data-augmented non-equivariant models against equivariant models
Tested both pointwise and nonlocal architectures at matched parameter counts
Evaluated spatiotemporal, anisotropy, and Reynolds number generalization in turbulent channel flow
evidence_signal: The equivariant nonlocal model achieved the highest correlation on every generalization test at about half the parameter count of its non-equivariant counterpart, while pointwise models did not beat the Clark baseline.
watch_item: Benefits were strongest for the larger receptive-field models, so gains may be limited if the closure architecture is too local or if training data are not sufficiently diverse.
paper_title: Rotational equivariance and locality in data-driven subgrid-scale closures
